mainTopic: Delaying and timing the כהן's inspection of נגעים, then the משנה on gathering parents' bones and mourning before a רגל
overview: This amud finishes a discussion about why the תורה needs two פסוקים, one about נגעים on the body and one about נגעים on a house, to teach that the כהן's inspection can sometimes be delayed. רבי shows that each פסוק teaches something the other could not. The גמרא then asks how the ברייתא learns from "וּבְיוֹם" that there are days when the כהן does not inspect. אביי learns it from the extra letter ו, and רבא learns it from the whole word. They then trace where each one learns that נגעים are inspected only by day: אביי from "בְּיוֹם", and רבא from "נִרְאָה לִי". Next comes a new משנה. רבי מאיר allows gathering one's parents' bones on חול המועד, while רבי יוסי calls it mourning. The משנה also bans stirring up mourning or giving a הספד in the thirty days before a רגל. The גמרא answers a challenge to רבי מאיר through אביי, explains what "arousing" mourning means, and gives רב's story behind the thirty days. שמואל's answer begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: House impurity is a special rule, so we cannot learn from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that נגעי בתים are a חידוש: wood and stones are normally never טמא, yet here they become טמא. So the house case cannot teach us about the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: For wood and stones normally do not become impure, yet here they do become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the house cannot teach the body: wood and stones are normally never טמא, yet in a house with צרעת they are, so this is a חידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, building materials like wood and stone cannot become טמא at all. The fact that a house can get צרעת is a חידוש. We have a rule that you cannot build other laws on top of a חידוש, so the body case needs its own פסוק, "וּבְיוֹם הֵרָאוֹת בּוֹ".

keyTerms.meaning: Wood and stones, the materials a house is built from
Generally, in every other case
They become ritually impure
A novel, unusual law that goes against the normal rules

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a house is not really טמא. It is טמא. The point is only that this is an unusual rule, so other laws cannot be learned from it.

phrases.english: For wood and stones
generally do not become impure,
yet here they do become impure.
phrases.notes: "Here" means a house that has צרעת.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא עֵצִים וַאֲבָנִים בְּעָלְמָא לָא מִטַּמְּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's answer why he does not derive a body's optional delay from house impurity.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the source case is a חידוש and cannot be used to derive other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought we could learn the body case from the house case.
steps.terutzMaskana: House impurity is a חידוש, so the body case needs its own פסוק.

steps.title: רבי explains why the house verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי says both פסוקים are necessary. If we only had "וּבְיוֹם הֵרָאוֹת בּוֹ", we would think delaying the inspection is allowed only for a דבר מצוה, not for a דבר הרשות. So the תורה wrote "וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי said: Both were needed. If the Merciful One had written only "And on the day it appears in him," I would have said that for a מצוה matter, yes, we may delay, but for an optional matter, no. So the Merciful One wrote "And the כהן shall command."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different way to explain why we need both פסוקים. He starts by showing what we would have wrongly thought if we only had the body פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body פסוק teaches that a חתן may delay the inspection during his wedding week, which is a מצוה reason. From that alone we might limit delays to מצוה reasons. The house פסוק ("וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן וּפִנּוּ אֶת הַבַּיִת") lets the owner delay just to empty out his belongings, an optional reason, so it widens the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (both verses are needed)
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
A matter of מצוה, a religious obligation
An optional, personal matter
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: And רבי said: It was necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written
"And on the day it appears in him,"
I would have said: for a מצוה matter, yes,
for an optional matter, no,
so the Merciful One wrote "And the כהן shall command."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:36. The owner may wait so he can empty out his house, which is not a מצוה reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of why both פסוקים are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each פסוק teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the body פסוק, we would think we may delay only for a מצוה reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The house פסוק teaches that even an optional reason allows a delay.

steps.title: Why the body verse is still needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי finishes the צריכותא. If we only had "וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן", we would allow delay only for a house, where the owner's body is not טמא. For טומאה of the body itself we would think the כהן must inspect right away. So both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written only "And the כהן shall command," I would have said: for these (the house items), yes, since this is not impurity of his body. But for impurity of his body, I would say the כהן must inspect it right away. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי shows the other side: what we would have wrongly thought with only the house פסוק. He ends by saying "צריכא", meaning both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house נגע only affects a person's belongings, so being lenient there is easier. A נגע on the body makes the person himself טמא, which is more serious, so we might have required an immediate inspection. The body פסוק teaches that a delay is allowed even there.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of his own body
He must definitely inspect it (right away)
It is necessary (both are needed). This closes a צריכותא

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק teaches something the other cannot. The house פסוק allows delay even for an optional reason. The body פסוק allows delay even when the person's own body is involved. Together they make the full law.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written "And the כהן shall command,"
I would have said: for these, yes,
phrases.notes: "These" means the things inside the house that the owner wants to save.

phrases.english: since it is not impurity of his body,
but impurity of his body —
I would say he must definitely inspect it.
It is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״וְצִוָּה הַכֹּהֵן״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רבי's צריכותא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the house פסוק, we would require an immediate inspection for a body נגע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The body פסוק allows delay even for טומאה of the body, so both פסוקים are needed.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא to begin analyzing it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and quotes its opening line: there is a day you inspect and a day you do not. This sets up the analysis that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: There is a day when you inspect him, and there is a day when you do not inspect him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can discuss that line next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word "וּבְיוֹם" ("and on the day") as hinting that only some days are for inspecting. On other days, like a חתן's wedding week, the inspection is pushed off. The גמרא is about to ask questions about this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Inspects or examines (the נגע)

phrases.english: The Master said:
There is a day when you inspect him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ יוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה רוֹאֶה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and there is a day when you do not inspect him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about why two פסוקים are needed and returns to analyze the ברייתא directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From "וּבְיוֹם הֵרָאוֹת בּוֹ" we learn that some days are for inspecting a נגע and some days are not.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק "וּבְיוֹם הֵרָאוֹת בּוֹ" teaches that some days you inspect and some days you do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What in the verse shows this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where in the פסוק we see the idea from the ברייתא that inspection can sometimes be delayed. This question sets up the answers of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a simple reading, "on the day it appears" sounds like the כהן must always inspect right away. So the גמרא wants to know which word in the פסוק allows a delay.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? Where in the verse is it hinted?

phrases.english: What shows this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's opening line, which was quoted in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the פסוק teaches that inspection can sometimes be delayed.

steps.title: אביי: the extra letter vav teaches it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the תורה could have written "בְּיוֹם". The extra ו in "וּבְיוֹם" teaches that some days you inspect and some days you do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If the כהן always had to inspect right away, the תורה should have written just "on the day." Why does it say "and on the day"? Learn from this: there is a day you inspect, and there is a day you do not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the extra letter ו ("and") at the start of "וּבְיוֹם" is the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain "בְּיוֹם" would mean that every day of appearance is a day of inspection. The added ו makes the rule depend on other factors, so some days, like a groom's wedding week or a יום טוב, are not inspection days.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה should have written
Learn from this
"And on the day", the word in the פסוק

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If so, the Merciful One should have written "on the day"
Why "and on the day"?
Learn from this:
there is a day when you inspect him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ יוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה רוֹאֶה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and there is a day when you do not inspect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִם כֵּן לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״בְּיוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in "וּבְיוֹם" teaches that inspection is sometimes delayed.

steps.title: רבא: the whole word "on the day" is extra
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the whole word "וּבְיוֹם" is extra, because the תורה could have written just "וּבְהֵרָאוֹת". That extra word teaches the delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The whole phrase is extra. If the כהן always had to inspect right away, the תורה should have written just "and when it appears." Why add "and on the day"? Learn from this: there is a day you inspect, and there is a day you do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He says the entire word "וּבְיוֹם" is extra, not just the letter ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, "וּבְהֵרָאוֹת" ("and when it appears") would have been enough to command an inspection. Adding a whole word about "the day" points to a day-based condition: some days are for inspecting and some are not.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra, seemingly unneeded part of the verse, used to teach something
"And when it appears", the shorter wording the תורה could have used

phrases.english: Rava said:
The whole phrase is extra,
phrases.notes: He means the whole word "וּבְיוֹם", not just the letter ו like אביי.

phrases.english: for if so, the Merciful One should have written "and when it appears"
Why "and on the day"?
Learn from this:
there is a day when you inspect him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ יוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה רוֹאֶה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and there is a day when you do not inspect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כּוּלָּהּ קְרָא יַתִּירָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 5 that disagrees with אביי about which part of the פסוק is extra.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The whole word "וּבְיוֹם" is extra and teaches that inspection is sometimes delayed.

steps.title: אביי uses "on the day" for daytime only
steps.stepSummary: Why doesn't אביי learn like רבא from the word "בְּיוֹם"? Because he needs it to teach that inspection happens by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He needs that word to teach: by day, and not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי does not use the whole word "בְּיוֹם" the way רבא does. For him the word teaches a different rule: inspection only by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word must teach something. אביי already uses "בְּיוֹם" for the daytime rule, so only the letter ו is left over to teach the delay.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs that word for something else
By day and not at night

phrases.english: And Abaye? He needs that one
phrases.notes: "That one" is the word "בְּיוֹם", which רבא treated as extra.

phrases.english: for: by day and not at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אביי does not accept רבא's reading from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is already used for another rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "בְּיוֹם" looks extra, so אביי should learn the delay from it like רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי needs "בְּיוֹם" to teach that inspection is only by day.

steps.title: Where does רבא learn "by day, not at night"?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבא used "וּבְיוֹם" for the delay, the גמרא asks where he learns that inspection is only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, where does he learn "by day and not at night"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבא. He used up the word "וּבְיוֹם" for the delay, so where does he get the daytime rule? This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that inspection is only by day. The question is only about the source, because רבא already used the word that אביי uses for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא, בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rava, from where does he learn "by day and not at night"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same check from אביי to רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבא's source for the rule that inspection happens only during the day.

steps.title: רבא learns it from "the sight of the כהן's eyes"
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns the daytime rule from "לְכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן": the כהן must see clearly, which needs daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "as far as the כהן's eyes can see."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא learns the daytime rule from a different פסוק about the כהן's eyesight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן" mean the inspection depends on the כהן's full, clear sight. That cannot happen properly at night, so רבא does not need "בְּיוֹם" for this.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
"As far as the כהן's eyes can see"

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״לְּכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן״.
phrases.english: He derives it from "as far as the priest's eyes can see."

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״לְּכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא learns the daytime rule from "לְכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן".

steps.title: אביי uses that verse to exclude a one-eyed כהן
steps.stepSummary: Why doesn't אביי learn the daytime rule from "מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן"? Because he needs it to exclude a כהן who is blind in one eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He needs that פסוק to exclude a כהן who is blind in one eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי does not use רבא's source. He needs "עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן" for a different rule: a כהן blind in one eye cannot inspect נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Eyes" is plural, so the כהן must see with both eyes. For אביי that is what this פסוק teaches, so his daytime rule must come from "בְּיוֹם". The next step asks whether רבא also needs this פסוק for the one-eyed כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
Blind in one of his eyes

steps.whatToRemember: Both agree that inspection can sometimes be delayed, that it is done only by day, and that a one-eyed כהן cannot inspect. They argue only about sources. For אביי: the ו teaches the delay, "בְּיוֹם" teaches daytime, and "עֵינֵי" excludes a one-eyed כהן. For רבא: "וּבְיוֹם" teaches the delay. The next steps show that he too uses "עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן" for the one-eyed כהן, and learns daytime from "נִרְאָה לִי".

phrases.english: And Abaye? He needs that one
to exclude one who is blind in one of his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי, הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי סוֹמֵא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אביי does not accept רבא's source from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is already used for another rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי could learn the daytime rule from "מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן" like רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי needs that פסוק to exclude a כהן blind in one eye.

steps.title: Doesn't רבא also need that verse for the one-eyed priest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: he also needs 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' to exclude a one-eyed כהן, so how can he use it for the daytime rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא also needs that פסוק for this, doesn't he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. The פסוק he used for 'daytime only' is also needed to exclude a כהן who is blind in one eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, אביי used 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' to exclude a one-eyed כהן. That rule is not only אביי's opinion; רבא must hold it too. One פסוק normally cannot be stretched to teach both rules, so רבא's source for the daytime rule looks shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
For this purpose

phrases.english: But doesn't Rava also need it for this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns אביי's answer from Step 11 into a challenge against רבא's source from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' as the source for 'by day only'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used to exclude a one-eyed כהן, a rule רבא must also hold, so it cannot also serve as his daytime source.

steps.title: Yes, רבא agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבא also uses that פסוק for the one-eyed כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not fight the challenge. It agrees that רבא also uses 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' for the one-eyed כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a concession. It drops what רבא was said to hold in Step 10, so he now has no source for the daytime rule. That gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Indeed it is so (a concession)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא gives up the daytime rule. The גמרא only admits that 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' is not his source for it. Step 15 gives his real source.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבא also use 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' for the one-eyed כהן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, he does, so it is not his source for the daytime rule.

steps.title: Then where does רבא learn 'day and not night'?
steps.stepSummary: Since that פסוק is taken, the גמרא asks where רבא gets the rule that נגעים are inspected only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, where does he learn 'by day and not at night'?
steps.whatsHappening: After the concession, רבא is left without a source for inspecting only by day. The גמרא asks where he gets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used 'וּבְיוֹם' for the delay (Step 7), and now 'מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן' is used for the one-eyed כהן. He needs a third source. This is a real search for information, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then (since the earlier answer fell away)
By day and not at night
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: If so, by day and not at night
from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the concession in Step 13, which left רבא's daytime rule without a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבא's source for inspecting נגעים only by day

steps.title: 'Seen by me' and not by my lamp
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns the daytime rule from the פסוק about נגעי בתים: 'נִרְאָה לִי' means seen by me, not by my light.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'something like a נגע has appeared to me in the house.' 'To me' and not to my lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא learns the daytime rule from the פסוק where a homeowner tells the כהן a נגע has appeared in his house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'לִי' ('to me') is read as 'seen by my own eyes in natural light', not by a lamp I light. So a נגע is judged only in daylight.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
'Something like a נגע has appeared to me in the house' (about נגעי בתים)
By my light (a lamp or candle)

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״כְּנֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת״.
phrases.english: He derives it from 'something like a plague has appeared to me in the house.'
'To me': and not to my light.
phrases.notes: He means seen in daylight with my own eyes, not by a lamp I light at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״כְּנֶגַע נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'נִרְאָה לִי' in the פרשה of נגעי בתים: by me, not by my lamp, so daytime only.

steps.title: Why אביי still needs his own source
steps.stepSummary: אביי does not learn from the house פסוק, because from there one might think only house-נגעים need daylight. A נגע on a person's body might be seen even by lamplight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? If we learned it from there, I would have said this applies only to a טומאה that is not on the body. But a טומאה on the body might be checked even by lamplight. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי needs his own source, 'וּבְיוֹם', from the פסוק about a person's skin, instead of using רבא's house פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house נגע is a טומאה not on the person's own body. Someone might think a body נגע is more serious and can be checked right away, even by lamplight. So אביי needs a פסוק written about the body itself to teach that it too must be checked only by day.

keyTerms.meaning: If we learned it from there, I would have thought
A טומאה not on one's own body (here, a house נגע)
A טומאה on one's own body (a skin נגע)
It teaches us (that the mistaken thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Both agree that נגעים are checked only by day. רבא learns it from 'נִרְאָה לִי' about houses. אביי learns it from 'וּבְיוֹם' about the body, because the house פסוק alone might not cover a person's body.

phrases.english: And Abaye? If from there, I would have said:
phrases.notes: 'From there' is רבא's house פסוק, 'נִרְאָה לִי בַּבָּיִת'.

phrases.english: this applies to an impurity that is not of his body,
but an impurity of his body
may be checked even by his light too,
so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is אביי's פסוק 'וּבְיוֹם', written about a נגע on a person's skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question: why doesn't אביי simply use רבא's source from Step 15?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the second source is needed: the house פסוק alone would not cover body נגעים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only house נגעים need daylight; a body נגע could be checked even by lamplight.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וּבְיוֹם', said about the body, teaches that body נגעים are also checked only by day.

steps.title: New משנה: gathering parents' bones on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי מאיר says a person may gather the bones of his father and mother on חול המועד, because it is a joy for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי מאיר also said: A person may gather the bones of his father and mother, because it is a joy for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה with another ruling of רבי מאיר about what is allowed on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering a parent's bones for final burial looks like mourning, which does not fit the festival. רבי מאיר allows it because bringing one's parents to their final resting place gives the son a feeling of joy.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
And he also said (another ruling from the same Sage)
Gathers bones (moving the remains to final burial)
Joy

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason 'joy' sets up the coming discussion. The question is whether gathering bones is a joyful act that fits חול המועד, or a mournful one.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And Rabbi Meir also said:
A person may gather the bones of his father and his mother,
because it is a joy for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the נגעים discussion and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one may gather his parents' bones on חול המועד because it is a joy for him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: gathering bones is mourning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר. Gathering a parent's bones brings mourning, so it should not be done on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It is mourning for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the argument from step 17. רבי יוסי says gathering a parent's bones is a sad thing, not a happy one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allowed ליקוט עצמות on חול המועד because it is a joy, since the parents finally get a proper burial. רבי יוסי says the main feeling is mourning, because it reminds the son of their death. Mourning does not fit the רגל, so he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It is mourning for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֵבֶל הוּא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathering a parent's bones counts as mourning, so it is forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: No eulogy in the thirty days before a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may not stir up mourning or give a הספד for his dead relative during the thirty days before a רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not stir up mourning for his dead relative, and may not eulogize him, during the thirty days before the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule. Even before the רגל begins, a person may not start fresh mourning or a הספד for his dead relative in the last thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about a relative who died some time ago. Stirring up the mourning again close to the רגל could leave a person sad when the רגל arrives. So the משנה keeps this kind of mourning out of the thirty days before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Arouse, stir up (here, stirring up mourning)
He will eulogize him
A pilgrimage Festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
Thirty days

phrases.english: A person may not stir up [mourning] over his dead relative,
phrases.notes: The word 'mourning' is not written, but that is what he would be stirring up.

phrases.english: and he may not eulogize him
during the thirty days before the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule in the משנה, still about keeping mourning away from the רגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No stirring up mourning and no הספד for one's dead during the thirty days before a רגל.

steps.title: A ברייתא says gathering bones brings a day of mourning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר. A ברייתא says one who gathers his parents' bones mourns for them all that day, and רב חסדא adds that this is true even if the bones were already wrapped in a sheet. So gathering bones is clearly mourning, not joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: They raised a contradiction: One who gathers the bones of his father and mother mourns for them the whole day, but in the evening he does not mourn for them. And רב חסדא said: Even if they were bundled up for him in his sheet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבי מאיר. If gathering a parent's bones makes a person mourn all day, how can רבי מאיר call it a joy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allowed ליקוט עצמות on חול המועד because it is a joy. The ברייתא says it causes a full day of mourning. רב חסדא makes the challenge stronger: even when the son does not have to dig the bones up, burying them still brings mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction
One who gathers bones for reburial
Mourns
Bundled up in his sheet

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The contradiction is against רבי מאיר from step 17, who called gathering bones a joy.

phrases.english: One who gathers the bones of his father and his mother —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מִתְאַבֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: he mourns for them the whole day,
but in the evening he does not mourn for them.
And Rav Chisda said:
Even if they were bundled up for him in his sheet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי מאיר's ruling from step 17 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reason that gathering a parent's bones is a joy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the son mourns all day after gathering his parents' bones, even if they were already wrapped. So the act is mourning, not joy.

steps.title: אביי: the Festival's joy covers the sadness
steps.stepSummary: אביי rereads רבי מאיר's reason. Gathering the bones is allowed on חול המועד not because the act itself is happy, but because the joy of the רגל is upon him and outweighs the sadness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Say instead, because the joy of the Festival is upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing how we read רבי מאיר's reason. The joy comes from the רגל, not from gathering the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is right that gathering bones normally brings mourning. רבי מאיר still permits it on חול המועד because the joy of the רגל is stronger and pushes the sadness aside. Now the ברייתא and רבי מאיר no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way instead)
The joy of the Festival

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, gathering a parent's bones really is sad. רבי מאיר allows it on חול המועד because the joy of the רגל outweighs that sadness.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying that gathering bones is a happy thing. He agrees it brings mourning. The joy he means is the joy of the רגל itself.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Say [instead],
because the joy of the Festival is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by rereading the משנה from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the reason given in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר meant that gathering a parent's bones is itself a happy act, which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר meant that the joy of the רגל outweighs the sadness of gathering the bones, so there is no clash with the ברייתא.

steps.title: What does 'arousing mourning for one's dead' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'ולא יערער על מתו' and asks what kind of act it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not arouse mourning for his dead.' What does this mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up רב's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two bans: not to 'arouse' (יערער) and not to give a הספד. A הספד is clear, but 'arousing' is vague. The גמרא wants to know what this separate act actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: Stir up or arouse mourning and crying
His dead relative
What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: And one may not arouse mourning for his dead.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 19.

phrases.english: What does 'one may not arouse mourning for his dead' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the discussion of gathering bones, the גמרא turns to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word יערער in the משנה.

steps.title: רב explains with the eulogizer's call in the West
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that in ארץ ישראל, a eulogizer going around would call out: 'Let all those with bitter hearts cry with him.' That call stirs up everyone's old grief.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: In the West (ארץ ישראל), when the eulogizer went around, they would say: 'Let everyone with a bitter heart cry with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by describing a real custom. The eulogizer invited everyone who was hurting to join the crying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Arousing' is not a full הספד for one person. It is a call that wakes up the pain of everyone who lost someone. That is why it is banned before a רגל, since it spreads sadness to many people.

keyTerms.meaning: A professional eulogizer
'The West', meaning ארץ ישראל
People with bitter hearts, those in pain over a loss

phrases.english: Rav said:
When the eulogizer would go around in the West,
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how the בבלי refers to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: they would say:
Let all those of bitter heart weep with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כַּד הָדַר סַפְדָנָא בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Arousing' is the eulogizer's public call for everyone in pain to weep along, which stirs up grief.

steps.title: Why exactly thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'thirty days before the רגל' from the משנה and asks why this specific length of time was chosen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Thirty days before the רגל.' What is special about thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the time limit from the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up two answers, first רב's and then שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might expect the ban on mourning to apply only on the רגל itself. The משנה pushes it back a whole month, so the גמרא wants to know why that number.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the three pilgrimage festivals
What is different / what is special about

phrases.english: Thirty days before the festival.
What is special about thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of יערער to the time limit in the same line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the ban begins thirty days before the רגל.

steps.title: The story of the man who lost his festival money
steps.stepSummary: רב tells of a man who saved money to go up to the רגל. A eulogizer came to his door, his wife gave him the money, and the man could not go. Because of this, the rule was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of רב: A man gathered money to go up for the רגל. A eulogizer came and stood at his door, and his wife took the money and gave it to him. The man held back and did not go up. At that time they said: one may not arouse mourning or give a הספד for his dead thirty days before the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers with a story from which the rule came. The money saved for the רגל was spent on a eulogizer, so the man missed the pilgrimage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is not only sadness but also money. A הספד before the רגל can use up the funds a person prepared for going up to ירושלים. The rule was made right after this event to stop it from happening again.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
To go up to ירושלים for the festival
A professional eulogizer
Held back, was prevented

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said that Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
There was an incident with one man
who gathered money to go up for the festival,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא סַפְדָן וְעָמַד עַל פֶּתַח בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: and a eulogizer came and stood at the entrance of his house,
and his wife took the money and gave it to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the eulogizer. She paid him with the money saved for the trip.

phrases.english: and the man held back and did not go up.
At that time they said:
One may not arouse mourning for his dead

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יַסְפִּידֶנּוּ קוֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: nor eulogize him thirty days before the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁכִּינֵּס מָעוֹת לַעֲלוֹת לָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's answer to the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The thirty-day ban was made after a הספד used up a man's festival money, so he missed the pilgrimage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the ban protects a person's ability to go up for the רגל, not only the happy mood of the festival.

steps.title: שמואל begins a different answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces שמואל, who will give his own reason for the thirty days. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only introduces שמואל. The גמרא is setting up a second answer to 'why thirty days', which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב gave a reason based on a story, שמואל is about to offer another explanation. His actual reason comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second answer to the question of step 24, next to רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given; שמואל's reason follows in the continuation.
